Voxlocal: a minimal voice agent written in Rust
items.summary_en: Voxlocal is an open-source, fully local voice agent for macOS written in Rust that processes speech through a transparent pipeline: microphone capture → Whisper STT → cosine-similarity RAG retrieval → LLM action routing → Piper TTS. It deliberately skips complex async streaming and voice-activity detection, instead using bare-bones off-the-shelf components to keep each step inspectable, targeting an English automotive-service use case. The project (samkhawase/voxlocal) demonstrates that a functional, low-latency conversational agent can be built with minimal dependencies and plain Rust for tool execution.

items.title: Byte Language Models: Scaling, Emergent Abstractions, and Information Allocation
items.summary_en: Byte Transformers using token-superposition training and hash embeddings outperform traditional subword models as parameters scale, developing implicit local abstractions without specialized architectures. These byte models achieve speculative decoding efficiency gains—roughly 3.4× more accepted tokens per forward pass—and show ~40% better performance on CUTE word manipulation and a 20% boost on OCRBench compared to subword counterparts. The research suggests future architectures may replace rigid subword vocabularies with flat Transformers combined with sparse mixture-of-experts for dynamic compute allocation, particularly benefiting multimodal applications.
